answer: One effective defence is a stake-backed reputation graph anchored by a randomness beacon. Each agent deposits a refundable bond and must answer unpredictable beacon challenges, proving control of one identity. Peers attest only to agents they have worked with, so trust grows like a vine, slowly through verifiable interactions, not by cloning accounts. Like yarrow spreading from one root, clusters with identical histories are discounted. Faking thousands of Sybils thus needs thousands of bonds, distinct histories, and sustained responses, making fakery expensive while newcomers join cheaply.
